name: Cholera
transmission: Vibrio cholerae bacteria contamination from sewage
recommendations: Immediately stop consuming water from this source for drinking or cooking.
Boil water at a rapid rolling boil for at least 3-5 minutes before domestic use.
Disinfect the water source with bleaching powder (chlorine treatment) immediately.
Administer Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) and seek urgent medical care at a hospital.

name: Typhoid Fever
transmission: Salmonella typhi bacteria in feces contaminated water
recommendations: Do not consume untreated water from this source.
Use certified water purification methods (chlorine disinfection or boiling).
Maintain strict personal hygiene and sanitize food preparation utensils.
Consult a doctor for diagnostic blood tests and antibiotic treatment.

name: Acute Gastroenteritis (E. coli / Rotavirus)
transmission: Pathogenic microbial pathogens from fecal pollution
recommendations: Filter water using a sub-micron filter and boil before consumption.
Add chlorine liquid drops to household water storage vessels.
Ensure water storage containers are tightly covered and cleaned regularly.
Keep patient hydrated using clean boiled water with ORS.

name: Amoebic Dysentery (Amoebiasis)
transmission: Entamoeba histolytica protozoan parasite cysts
recommendations: Filter water through a fine sand/ceramic filter to capture cysts, then boil it.
Avoid raw uncooked vegetables washed in this water source.
Thoroughly clean overhead tanks and household water storage systems.
Visit the health center for anti-parasitic treatment prescriptions.

name: Hepatitis A / E
transmission: Fecal-oral viral contamination of public water systems
recommendations: Strictly boil all drinking and cooking water; viruses are resistant to mild chlorine.
Avoid communal open water storage systems.
Vaccinate susceptible family members against Hepatitis A.
Seek medical advice immediately for liver function evaluation.

name: Dental/Skeletal Fluorosis
transmission: High naturally occurring inorganic fluoride minerals in deep aquifers
recommendations: Avoid consuming raw borewell water; use activated alumina filters or RO plants.
Mix borewell water with rain-harvested water to reduce fluoride concentration.
Avoid using high-fluoride toothpaste in children and consume a calcium-rich diet.
Visit local health officers for skeletal fluorosis physical screening.

name: Arsenicosis (Arsenic Toxicity)
transmission: Geogenic arsenic contamination in groundwater
recommendations: Never consume water from wells marked with red alert signs.
Filter water using iron-coagulation filters or specialized arsenic removal cartridges.
Promote community rain-water harvesting as an alternate drinking source.
Seek specialized dermatological screening for keratosis and skin lesions.

name: Chemical Lead Contamination
transmission: Corroding lead service lines or industrial effluent leakage
recommendations: Run municipal taps for 2 minutes before using water to flush standing lead.
Use only cold water for cooking and baby formula; hot water dissolves lead faster.
Use certified lead-removing filters (look for NSF/ANSI Standard 53).
Consult local pediatric clinics to check blood lead levels in children.

name: Giardiasis
transmission: Giardia lamblia parasite cysts in feces-contaminated fresh water
recommendations: Filter water using a filter certified for cyst removal (NSF 53/58).
Boil water for at least 1 minute (or 3 minutes at higher altitudes) to kill cysts.
Avoid raw foods that cannot be peeled, or wash them in boiled water.
Consult a health practitioner for stool tests and anti-protozoal medication.

name: Cryptosporidiosis
transmission: Cryptosporidium oocysts resistant to typical chlorine treatment
recommendations: Boil water to kill oocysts; typical chlorination alone is highly ineffective.
Use a filtration unit with an absolute pore size of 1 micron or smaller.
Isolate clinical patients and prevent swimming to avoid municipal spread.
Seek medical advice immediately for fluid management and recovery check.

name: Shigellosis (Bacillary Dysentery)
transmission: Shigella bacterial contamination via fecal-oral vector
recommendations: Immediately sanitize water systems and discard untreated standing storage.
Treat household water with chlorine disinfection and subsequent boiling.
Wash hands vigorously with soap before food preparation.
Visit the primary health center for antibiotic susceptibility testing.

name: Legionnaires' Disease
transmission: Inhalation of aerosols from water systems contaminated with Legionella
recommendations: Regularly disinfect overhead water storage tanks and warm water systems (above 60°C).
Clean and descale showerheads, tap aerators, and cooling systems.
Avoid generating water spray or mist from suspect municipal reservoirs.
Seek diagnostic evaluation for atypical pneumonia symptoms.

name: Schistosomiasis (Bilharzia)
transmission: Cercariae larvae released by freshwater snails penetrating skin
recommendations: Avoid wading, bathing, or washing clothes in untreated surface water.
Boil water for domestic bathing/washing, or store it for 48 hours to kill cercariae.
Implement snail control measures near agricultural water canals.
Seek medical testing and treatment with Praziquantel if exposure is confirmed.

name: Leptospirosis
transmission: Leptospira spirochete bacteria excreted in rodent/animal urine
recommendations: Boil and chlorinate all drinking water. Discard flood-affected open reserves.
Avoid contact with water that might be contaminated with animal urine.
Cover skin wounds with waterproof dressings before touching water.
Consult doctors immediately for early doxycycline/penicillin regimens.

name: Microcystin Toxicity (Blue-Green Algal Blooms)
transmission: Cyanobacteria toxins released during massive algal blooms
recommendations: Never consume, swim, or wash in water affected by blue-green algal blooms.
Do not boil water to treat toxins; boiling breaks cells and releases more toxin.
Use active carbon filtration combined with reverse osmosis for treatment.
Consult medical officers for skin rashes or liver function checks if ingested.

name: Nitrate Contamination (Blue Baby Syndrome)
transmission: Nitrate leaching from chemical fertilizers or animal manure
recommendations: Do not feed infant formula using this well water; nitrates cause methemoglobinemia.
Do not boil water to remove nitrates; boiling increases their concentration.
Install ion exchange or reverse osmosis systems to eliminate nitrates.
Seek immediate medical care if an infant shows blue or purple skin discoloration.

name: Cadmium Toxicity (Itai-Itai Disease)
transmission: Heavy metal runoff from industrial waste and zinc mines
recommendations: Cease using water for drinking or agricultural irrigation immediately.
Install heavy-metal removing filtration systems (RO or carbon blocks).
Conduct mass-spectrometry chemical testing of the local well network.
Consult a rheumatologist or toxicologist for heavy metal body burden checks.

name: Agricultural Pesticide Poisoning
transmission: Runoff of organophosphate/carbamate chemicals from farms
recommendations: Do not consume water with chemical smell; boiling does not deactivate pesticides.
Use high-grade activated carbon filtration systems.
Audit agricultural pesticide application boundaries near water bodies.
Seek emergency medical help if muscle twitching or breathing issues occur.

name: Copper Poisoning (Toxicity)
transmission: Corrosion of copper plumbing pipes or agricultural copper sprays
recommendations: Flush water system by running cold taps for 1 minute before domestic use.
Avoid storing acidic foods or water in copper containers.
Install reverse osmosis or copper-reducing filtration systems.
Check liver function tests if chronic gastrointestinal symptoms persist.

name: High Salinity / TDS Syndrome
transmission: Over-extraction of groundwater leading to saltwater intrusion
recommendations: Install reverse osmosis (RO) system to reduce Total Dissolved Solids (TDS).
Avoid using saline water for domestic irrigation as it damages soil structure.
Blend borewell water with rain-harvested water to improve quality.
Monitor blood pressure if consuming highly saline borewell water.
